Don’t Wait

Warning Signs You Need
a Septic or Plumbing Pro Now

Arizona’s desert heat accelerates septic problems. Ignoring early warning signs can turn a $200 pump-out into a $15,000 system replacement. If you’re seeing any of these, call before it gets worse.

01

Slow Drains Everywhere

One slow drain is usually a local clog. Multiple slow drains throughout the house points to a full or failing septic tank.

02

Sewage Odors Indoors

If you smell sulfur or sewage inside the home, your tank may be backing up or a vent pipe could be blocked.

03

Soggy Patches in the Yard

Wet or unusually green grass over the drain field indicates the leach field may be saturated and failing to absorb effluent.

04

Gurgling Toilets or Drains

Gurgling sounds when you flush or run water signal that air is trapped in the lines — often the first sign of a system under pressure.

05

Sewage Backup in Low Fixtures

Sewage coming up through floor drains or lowest-level toilets is a septic emergency. Call immediately — do not use any plumbing.

06

It’s Been 3+ Years Since Pumping

Arizona’s heat increases biological activity in the tank. Most homes need pumping every 2–3 years to prevent overflow and leach field damage.
